# Workout log

Log each training session, see your personal bests and how each exercise is going, and what's next in your plan.

**Read docs/ first.** It's this app's memory: what it's for, the shape of its data, the decisions made and why, and what's missing. Keep it current whenever you change the app.

## Screens
- Set up your training (src/screens/setup.tsx): a new log's first screen. The starting workouts are suggestions to tick, untick or rename, with the sessions a week and kg or lb; Start writes the plan and the log starts. Nothing is counted before it.
- Today (src/screens/today.tsx): this week's sessions against the weekly goal, what's next in the plan (each exercise with what it was last time) and Start, which opens the session already filled in. Then the latest sessions and the latest bests.
- Sessions (src/screens/log.tsx): every session by month, newest first; Log adds one, and choosing one opens it to change or delete (with Undo).
- Progress (src/screens/progress.tsx, src/components/chart.tsx): one exercise over time (estimated 1RM or heaviest set; distance or pace for cardio) and every exercise's personal best with its date.
- Plan (src/screens/plan.tsx): the workouts in the order they're done, the exercises, the units and the weekly goal: add, rename, reorder and remove (with Undo).

A session is logged and changed in src/components/session-sheet.tsx. The data, the units and the sums (bests, the week, what's next) are in src/lib/workouts.ts; the shared pieces (sections, rows, ring, sheet, pills) in src/components/kit.tsx.

## Tests
`npm test` runs Vitest. Tests live in tests/*.test.tsx and use Testing Library (render, screen, userEvent) with the jest-dom matchers; `amber` (from "amber") shows what was saved. A test can start over a sample of the app's data, so each test here sets the data it needs first (beforeEach). Pinto Notes runs them, and a quick check that the app opens and its buttons work, on every save: a version that fails isn't shown to the person; the last one that passed keeps running until the failures are fixed.

**Every feature you add gets a test like the ones in tests/app.test.tsx**: do what the person does, check what they see, and check what was saved. When the app changes on purpose, change its tests to match the new behaviour. Never weaken, skip or delete a test just to make it pass: fix the app instead.

## How this app runs in Pinto Notes

- It is the note: opening the note opens the app, on iPhone (320-440 pt wide, safe areas, the keyboard shrinks the view) and on the Mac (a window from about 500 to 1,800 px, resized live). Light and dark follow the device.
- A normal Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui project. Pinto Notes compiles it when a file is saved (TSX, the @/ alias, imports without extensions, Tailwind from the classes used) and says what broke; nothing is installed. React runs on preact/compat.
- Available by name: react, react-dom, radix-ui, lucide-react, recharts, date-fns, zod, motion, sonner, react-day-picker, clsx, tailwind-merge, class-variance-authority, amber-router (Router, Route, route(), back()), chart.js, d3, three, tone, dayjs, marked, dompurify, animejs, canvas-confetti.
- Data is JSON that Pinto Notes keeps for the app (encrypted, synced, with Undo): useStore(key, initial), useCollection(name), useSettings(defaults), batch(fn), setSummary(text) from "@/lib/amber". localStorage works too and is kept the same way. The person's AI reads and edits it as data.json, so keep its shape simple and describe it in docs/README.md.
- No network except hosts the person allows: declare them in index.html with <meta name="amber-needs" content='{"hosts": ["api.open-meteo.com"]}'> and call fetch(url) from "@/lib/amber"; API keys live in Pinto Notes › Settings › API Keys (declare { "keys": [{ "name", "hosts", "query" or "header" }] } and pass { key: name }).
- The device: device.openURL(url) opens a link once the person agrees to it, share(file) exports one, device.photos.pick() and device.files.pick() let the person choose. Reminders, Calendar, notifications, the camera, contacts, location, Maps and on-device AI are not available yet.

# Workout log: notes for whoever works on this app next

## What it's for
A person who trains a few times a week logs each session, often on their phone between sets or right after. They want to see their personal bests and whether they're getting stronger, and to know what's next. Their AI logs sessions for them too ("did 3x5 squats at 100 kg and a 5 km run"), says whether that was a best, and answers questions like "am I getting stronger on bench?".

## Data
data.json, all under "values" (the person's AI reads and edits it directly):
- exercises: [{ id, name, kind }]. kind is "weight" (sets of reps and weight) or "cardio" (distance and time). id is a lowercase slug of the name ("bench-press"). Renaming changes name, never id.
- plan: [{ id, name, exercises: [exercise id] }]. The workouts, in the order they're done in turn (Legs, Push, Pull, Easy run). Today shows the one after the last session's workout.
  - pick: false marks a suggestion that starts unticked on a new log's first screen. Only the starting data has it; Start doesn't save it.
- sessions: [{ id, date, name, workout?, effort?, note?, items }]. date is "yyyy-mm-dd"; name is what the person calls it ("Legs"); workout is the plan workout's id (missing is fine: a session whose name is a workout's name counts as that workout); effort is 1 to 10; note is a line of text. id is any unique text ("s" and a few letters is fine).
  - items: [{ exercise, sets }]. exercise is an id from exercises. A weight set is { reps, kg } (no kg: bodyweight, like pull-ups); a cardio set is { km, min } (either can be left out; min is minutes, 29.5 is 29:30).
  - **Weights are always kg and distances always km, whatever units says.** A person who says "225 lb" gets kg: 102.06 (lb ÷ 2.20462, two decimals); "3 miles" is km: 4.83.
- units: "kg" or "lb". What the app shows and takes. lb shows miles too. Missing: kg (the first screen guesses lb in the US).
- goal: sessions a week (1 to 14). Missing: 3.
- started: "yyyy-mm-dd". The day the log was set up. Missing is fine once anything is logged.

A new log has exercises (ten), a plan (four suggestions), goal 3, no units, no started and no sessions. **To set one up, write the person's plan (and any exercises it needs), goal and units, and set started to today's date.** Without started (and with no sessions) the app opens on Set up your training and treats the plan as suggestions.

To log a session, append to sessions with a new id. An exercise that isn't in exercises yet goes there first ({ id: slug of the name, name, kind }); the app shows an unknown id with a name made from it, so a missing one isn't lost.

### Personal bests
The app works them out from the sessions; nothing about them is stored. To tell the person whether a session was a best, do the same sums:
- Weight exercises: the estimated one-rep max (Epley) of the best set, weight × (1 + reps ÷ 30), and a single (1 rep) is its own weight. 100 kg × 5 is 116.7, so it beats 110 kg × 1. When no set of an exercise has a weight, the most reps in a set.
- Cardio: the longest distance in a session (its sets added up) and the fastest pace (time ÷ distance, from the sets that have both). Each is its own best.
- A session sets a new best when it beats every session before it (by date, then by order in the list). The first time an exercise is done sets its best but beats nothing, so it isn't marked.

## Decisions
- Today does one job: start the next workout. Start opens the session filled in with the plan's exercises and the sets each had last time, so logging a session like the last one is changing a number or two and Log session. Each exercise's line says what it was last time ("Last: 100 kg × 5") or "First time". The other workouts of the plan are pills over it, for a day that goes differently.
- What's next is the plan's workout after the last session that was one of its workouts (matched by workout, else by name); after the last of the plan it starts again from the first. A session today shows "Done today: Legs" and the card is titled Next time.
- The week runs Monday to Sunday and counts sessions, not workouts or minutes, against the weekly goal: a ring, "2 of 3 sessions", "1 to go" or "Goal met", and the days trained as filled letters. Days to come are never a miss.
- Bests are worked out every time from the sessions (src/lib/workouts.ts, records), never stored: editing or deleting a session can't leave a stale best behind, and the AI doesn't have to keep two places in step.
- One measure for a lift's best, the estimated 1RM, so 100 kg × 5 and 105 kg × 3 compare. Progress also charts the heaviest set. "New best" marks a session that beat an earlier best; the bar after Log session says which exercise ("Logged Legs. New best: Squat.").
- The chart: a point per session, oldest on the left, the last 24; filled dots are sessions that set a best. Up is always better, so pace is drawn with the scale turned over. The line is an SVG that stretches with the width; the dots and labels are HTML so they stay round and readable (src/components/chart.tsx).
- Units: stored in kg and km, shown and typed in kg or lb (lb also shows miles). Switching never changes the data, and the AI never has to know which is shown.
- Sets are typed in text fields with the decimal keypad on iPhone ("102,5" is read as 102.5). Times take "29", "29:30" or "1:05:00". A new set starts as a copy of the one before it. A set with no reps, or a run with no distance and no time, isn't saved, and an exercise with no sets is left out.
- The person is in control without the AI: log, edit and delete sessions (Undo); add, rename, reorder and remove exercises and workouts (Undo); add an exercise from inside a session; change the units and the weekly goal. Removing an exercise takes it out of the plan; its sessions keep it, and Undo brings back both.
- Sessions are in date order, newest first. A session's place is its date: changing the date moves it. Exercises in a session are moved with up and down in the session sheet.
- The first screen's frame is the same in the five template apps (kit.tsx, FirstScreen). Made with an AI, the person is asked the same thing in the app and in the chat; the quiet line ("Pick here, or tell your AI and it sets this up.") says either works. When the person's AI sets the log up while the first screen is open, the app leaves it by itself; if the person had changed anything there, a bar that stays offers it back ("Use mine"). Tested in tests/app.test.tsx, "First use".
- From 700 px Today has two columns (except between 900 and 1100 px, where the sidebar leaves too little room); from 1100 px Progress and Plan do too.
- Colour: one accent (Pinto's amber), and the danger red on Remove. The three ambers have one job each, as in the other template apps (src/index.css): `--amber-accent` for rings, dots and the chart, `text-link` for amber text, `bg-primary` for the primary button (white with a black label in the dark).
- The app sets the note's summary line to "2 of 3 sessions this week, next: Push".
- No text under 12 px (0.75rem), Apple's minimum. Tests check text that changes after an action (saving is async) inside waitFor, never on the first find.

## Known gaps
- No rest timer, no plate maths, and no program that adds weight by itself.
- Sessions on the same day can't be put in another order except by their date.
- No warm-up sets: every set counts toward a best.
- Doesn't read Apple Health or a watch, and can't export yet (share() could write a CSV).

import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from "vitest"
import { render, screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { amber } from "amber"
import { route } from "amber-router"
import App from "@/App"
import { guessUnits } from "@/screens/setup"
import { addDays, dayText, e1rm, iso, parseTime, shortDate, timeText, today, type Session } from "@/lib/workouts"

// Each test does what the person does, then checks what they see and what was saved in data.json.
const values = () => amber.data.values ?? {}
const day = iso(today())
const ago = (n: number) => iso(addDays(today(), -n))
const squat = { id: "squat", name: "Squat", kind: "weight" }
const lunges = { id: "lunges", name: "Lunges", kind: "weight" }
const bench = { id: "bench-press", name: "Bench press", kind: "weight" }
const pullups = { id: "pull-ups", name: "Pull-ups", kind: "weight" }
const run = { id: "run", name: "Run", kind: "cardio" }
const legs = { id: "legs", name: "Legs", exercises: ["squat", "lunges"] }
const push = { id: "push", name: "Push", exercises: ["bench-press"] }
const easy = { id: "easy-run", name: "Easy run", exercises: ["run"] }
const fives = (kg: number, n = 3) => Array.from({ length: n }, () => ({ reps: 5, kg }))
const session = (id: string, date: string, name: string, items: Session["items"], more: Partial<Session> = {}): Session =>
  ({ id, date, name, items, ...(name === "Legs" ? { workout: "legs" } : name === "Push" ? { workout: "push" } : {}), ...more })
const sessionsNow = (): Session[] => values().sessions ?? []

// Start each test from a log that was set up long ago, with a small plan and nothing logged,
// whatever data the app holds (a new log opens on Set up your training: see "First use").
beforeEach(async () => {
  route("/")
  await amber.store.set("exercises", [squat, lunges, bench, pullups, run])
  await amber.store.set("plan", [legs, push, easy])
  await amber.store.set("sessions", [])
  await amber.store.set("units", "kg")
  await amber.store.set("goal", 3)
  await amber.store.set("started", "2026-01-05")
})
// The sidebar (Mac) and the tab bar (iPhone) both have the screens' links; either one goes there.
const go = async (name: string) => userEvent.click((await screen.findAllByRole("link", { name }))[0])
const field = (name: string) => screen.getByLabelText(name) as HTMLInputElement
const retype = async (name: string, text: string) => { const el = field(name); await userEvent.clear(el); await userEvent.type(el, text) }

describe("Today", () => {
  it("shows what's next in the plan with last time's sets, and logs it from there", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [
      session("s1", ago(5), "Legs", [{ exercise: "squat", sets: fives(95) }]),
      session("s2", ago(3), "Push", [{ exercise: "bench-press", sets: fives(60) }]),
    ])
    await amber.store.set("plan", [legs, push])
    render(<App />)
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("next-name")).toHaveTextContent("Legs"))
    expect(screen.getByText("Last: 95 kg × 5")).toBeInTheDocument()
    expect(screen.getByText("First time")).toBeInTheDocument()
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Start Legs" }))
    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { name: "Log session" })).toBeInTheDocument()
    expect(field("Squat set 1 weight")).toHaveValue("95")
    expect(field("Squat set 3 reps")).toHaveValue("5")
    await retype("Squat set 3 weight", "100")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Log session" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(sessionsNow()).toHaveLength(3))
    const s = sessionsNow()[2]
    // Lunges had nothing typed: an exercise with no sets isn't saved.
    expect({ ...s, id: undefined }).toEqual({ date: day, name: "Legs", workout: "legs", items: [{ exercise: "squat", sets: [{ reps: 5, kg: 95 }, { reps: 5, kg: 95 }, { reps: 5, kg: 100 }] }] })
    expect(await screen.findByText("Logged Legs. New best: Squat.")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("goes round the plan: after Legs comes Push, and you can pick another", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [session("s1", ago(1), "Legs", [{ exercise: "squat", sets: fives(100) }])])
    render(<App />)
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("next-name")).toHaveTextContent("Push"))
    expect(screen.getByText("Next in your plan")).toBeInTheDocument()
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("radio", { name: "Easy run" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("next-name")).toHaveTextContent("Easy run"))
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Start Easy run" })).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("after the last workout of the plan, starts again from the first", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [session("s1", ago(2), "Easy run", [{ exercise: "run", sets: [{ km: 5, min: 30 }] }], { workout: "easy-run" })])
    render(<App />)
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("next-name")).toHaveTextContent("Legs"))
  })

  it("counts this week's sessions against the weekly goal, which you set under Plan", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [session("s1", day, "Legs", [{ exercise: "squat", sets: fives(100) }])])
    render(<App />)
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("week-count")).toHaveTextContent("1 of 3 sessions"))
    // It wraps on a narrow phone (320 pt): kept on one line, "3 of 3 sessions" ran out of its card.
    expect(screen.getByTestId("week-count").className).not.toContain("whitespace-nowrap")
    expect(screen.getByTestId("week-left")).toHaveTextContent("2 to go")
    expect(screen.getByRole("img", { name: "This week 1 of 3" })).toBeInTheDocument()
    await go("Plan")
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Fewer sessions a week" }))
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Fewer sessions a week" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().goal).toBe(1))
    await go("Today")
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("week-left")).toHaveTextContent("Goal met"))
  })

  it("says what was done today, and what's next time", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [session("s1", day, "Legs", [{ exercise: "squat", sets: fives(100) }])])
    render(<App />)
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("done-today")).toHaveTextContent("Done today: Legs"))
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "Next time" })).toBeInTheDocument()
    expect(screen.getByTestId("next-name")).toHaveTextContent("Push")
  })

  it("invites you to make a plan when there is none", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("plan", [])
    render(<App />)
    expect(await screen.findByText("No plan yet")).toBeInTheDocument()
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Make a plan" }))
    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { name: "Plan" })).toBeInTheDocument()
  })
})

describe("Logging a session", () => {
  it("logs a session by hand: an exercise, its sets, how hard it was and a note", async () => {
    render(<App />)
    await go("Sessions")
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Log" }))
    await retype("Workout", "Upper")
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Add exercise"), "Bench press")
    await userEvent.type(field("Bench press set 1 reps"), "8")
    await userEvent.type(field("Bench press set 1 weight"), "60")
    // A new set starts as a copy of the one before it.
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add a set to Bench press" }))
    expect(field("Bench press set 2 weight")).toHaveValue("60")
    await retype("Bench press set 2 reps", "6")
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("How hard (1 to 10)"), "7")
    await userEvent.type(field("Note"), "Felt strong")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Log session" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(sessionsNow()).toHaveLength(1))
    expect({ ...sessionsNow()[0], id: undefined }).toEqual({ date: day, name: "Upper", effort: 7, note: "Felt strong", items: [{ exercise: "bench-press", sets: [{ reps: 8, kg: 60 }, { reps: 6, kg: 60 }] }] })
    expect(await screen.findByText("Bench press 2 sets, best 60 kg × 8")).toBeInTheDocument()
    expect(screen.getByText("Effort 7")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("logs a run with its distance and time", async () => {
    render(<App />)
    await go("Sessions")
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Log" }))
    await retype("Workout", "Run")
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Add exercise"), "Run")
    await userEvent.type(field("Run set 1 distance"), "5")
    await userEvent.type(field("Run set 1 time"), "29:30")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Log session" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(sessionsNow()[0]?.items).toEqual([{ exercise: "run", sets: [{ km: 5, min: 29.5 }] }]))
    expect(await screen.findByText("Run 5 km in 29:30")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("makes a new exercise from the session, and keeps it for next time", async () => {
    render(<App />)
    await go("Sessions")
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Log" }))
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Add exercise"), "new")
    await userEvent.type(await screen.findByLabelText("New exercise"), "Hip thrust")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add Hip thrust" }))
    await userEvent.type(await screen.findByLabelText("Hip thrust set 1 reps"), "10")
    await userEvent.type(field("Hip thrust set 1 weight"), "80")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Log session" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().exercises.at(-1)).toEqual({ id: "hip-thrust", name: "Hip thrust", kind: "weight" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(sessionsNow()[0]?.items).toEqual([{ exercise: "hip-thrust", sets: [{ reps: 10, kg: 80 }] }]))
  })

  it("moves an exercise up, takes one out and removes a set", async () => {
    render(<App />)
    await go("Sessions")
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Log" }))
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Add exercise"), "Squat")
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Add exercise"), "Pull-ups")
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Add exercise"), "Bench press")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Move Bench press up" }))
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Take Squat out" }))
    await userEvent.type(field("Bench press set 1 reps"), "5")
    await userEvent.type(field("Bench press set 1 weight"), "70")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add a set to Bench press" }))
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Remove set 2 of Bench press" }))
    // Pull-ups with reps and no weight: a bodyweight set.
    await userEvent.type(field("Pull-ups set 1 reps"), "8")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Log session" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(sessionsNow()[0]?.items).toEqual([
      { exercise: "bench-press", sets: [{ reps: 5, kg: 70 }] },
      { exercise: "pull-ups", sets: [{ reps: 8 }] },
    ]))
  })

  it("changes a session: its name and a weight", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [session("s1", ago(2), "Legs", [{ exercise: "squat", sets: fives(100, 1) }])])
    render(<App />)
    await go("Sessions")
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: `Legs, ${dayText(ago(2))}` }))
    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { name: "Edit session" })).toBeInTheDocument()
    await retype("Workout", "Leg day")
    await retype("Squat set 1 weight", "102.5")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(sessionsNow()).toEqual([{ id: "s1", date: ago(2), name: "Leg day", workout: "legs", items: [{ exercise: "squat", sets: [{ reps: 5, kg: 102.5 }] }] }]))
    expect(await screen.findByText("Squat 102.5 kg × 5")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("deletes a session, and Undo brings it back", async () => {
    const s1 = session("s1", ago(2), "Legs", [{ exercise: "squat", sets: fives(100) }])
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [s1])
    route("/log")
    render(<App />)
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: `Legs, ${dayText(ago(2))}` }))
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Delete session" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(sessionsNow()).toEqual([]))
    expect(await screen.findByText("Deleted Legs")).toBeInTheDocument()

    route("/plan")
    render(<App />)
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "New workout" }))
    await userEvent.type(await screen.findByLabelText("Name"), "Upper")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Bench press" }))
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Pull-ups" }))
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add workout" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().plan.at(-1)).toEqual({ id: "upper", name: "Upper", exercises: ["bench-press", "pull-ups"] }))

    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Edit Legs" }))
    await retype("Name", "Lower")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().plan[0]).toEqual({ id: "legs", name: "Lower", exercises: ["squat", "lunges"] }))

    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Move Upper up" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().plan.map((w: { id: string }) => w.id)).toEqual(["legs", "push", "upper", "easy-run"]))
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Remove Push" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().plan.map((w: { id: string }) => w.id)).toEqual(["legs", "upper", "easy-run"]))
    expect(await screen.findByText("Removed Push")).toBeInTheDocument()
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Undo" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().plan.map((w: { id: string }) => w.id)).toEqual(["legs", "push", "upper", "easy-run"]))
  })

  it("adds, renames, reorders and removes exercises; a renamed one keeps its sessions and bests", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("sessions", [session("s1", ago(2), "Legs", [{ exercise: "squat", sets: fives(100) }])])
    route("/plan")

    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Edit Squat" }))

    await waitFor(() => expect(values().exercises[0]).toEqual({ id: "squat", name: "Back squat", kind: "weight" }))

    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Move Lunges up" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().exercises.slice(0, 2).map((e: { id: string }) => e.id)).toEqual(["lunges", "squat"]))

    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Remove Bench press" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().exercises.some((e: { id: string }) => e.id === "bench-press")).toBe(false))
    expect(values().plan.find((w: { id: string }) => w.id === "push").exercises).toEqual([])
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Undo" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().plan.find((w: { id: string }) => w.id === "push").exercises).toEqual(["bench-press"]))
    expect(values().exercises.some((e: { id: string }) => e.id === "bench-press")).toBe(true)

    await go("Progress")

    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: /^Back squat:/ })).toBeInTheDocument()

    expect(await screen.findByText("Squat 225 lb × 5")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("shows runs in miles once the units are lb", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("units", "lb")

    render(<App />)
    expect(await screen.findByText("Run 5 mi in 48:00")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })
})
